sentences.text: As per prosecution case in brief, complainant Incharge Inspector Shyam Singh Peelvan has lodged the instant F.I.R. dated 02.09.2020 against the applicant under Section 153A, 295A, 506 IPC and Section 67 Information Technology Act with the allegation inter alia that on 29.08.2020, after recovery of beef from the house in Hathighat and Dholakhar, a case was registered at Case Crime No. 88 of 2020, under Section 3/5A/8 of Cow Slaughter Act, Sections 188, 269, 270 of IPC, Section 11 of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act and Section 15 of Environment Protection Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As a result of lodging of the aforesaid F.I.R., the applicant in order to provoke the Muslim community got an alleged video viral, due to which there is tension in the locality between the two communities.
4-It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
Charge-sheet in this case has been wrongly filed by the police against the applicant, who is an Ex-State Minister, on the influence of the politicians of the ruling party.
The applicant has neither made any video viral nor given any speech regarding any religion.
Lastly, it is submitted that no offence is made out against the applicant.

Under the facts and circumstances of the case,
impugned charge-sheet, summoning order and criminal proceeding against the applicant is liable to be quashed by this Court.
5-Per contra, learned Additional Government Advocate for the State refuting the submissions advanced on behalf of the applicant submitted that the Investigating Officer of this case has collected the video, which was made viral by the applicant, and the said video along with required certificate under Section 65B of the Evidence Act have been made part of the case diary.

He also submits that upon perusal of F.I.R. and on the basis of the allegations made therein as well as material against the applicant, as per prosecution case, the cognizable offence against the applicant is made out.

He further submits that apart from this case, the applicant is having long criminal history of 14 cases, which are quoted herein below :
(i) Case Crime No. 078 of 2003, under Sections 147, 302, 396, 436, 452 IPC and Section 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, Police Station Mantola, Commissionerate Agra.
(ii) Case Crime No. 612 of 2003, under Section 304 IPC and Section 3(2)1 SC/ST Act,
Police Station Sadar Bazar, Commissionerate Agra.
(iii) Case Crime No. 003 of 2004, under Sections 147, 148, 149, 323, 307, 436 IPC and Section 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act and Section 7 Criminal Law Amendment Act, Police Station Mantola, Commissionerate Agra.
(iv) Case Crime No. 069 of 2007, under Section 188 IPC, Police Station Mantola,
Commissionerate Agra.
(v) Case Crime No. 275 of 2008, under Sections 409, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B IPC and Section 13(1)D Prevention of Corruption Act, Police Station Tajganj,
Commissionerate Agra.

On the strength of above argument, lastly it is submitted that the criminal proceedings against the applicant cannot be said to be abuse of the process of the Court.
Hence, this application is liable to be dismissed.
6-Having examined the matter in its totality, I find that the Investigating Officer has collected the video, which was made viral by the applicant and the same is also part of the case diary.
I also find that it is not dispute that the applicant have criminal history of 14 cases.
The grounds taken in the application reveal that many of them relate to disputed question of fact.
This Court is of the view that the appreciation of evidence is a function of the trial court.
This Court in exercise of power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. cannot assume such jurisdiction and put to an end to the process of trial provided under the law.

It is well settled by the Apex Court in catena of judgments that the power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. at pre-trial stage should not be used in a routine manner but it has to be used sparingly, only in such an appropriate cases, where it manifestly appears that there is a legal bar against the institution or continuance of the criminal proceedings or where allegations made in First Information Report or charge-sheet and the materials relied in support of same, on taking their face value and accepting in their entirety do not disclose the commission of any offence against the Chaudhary Vashir vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55601405/

sentences.text: The disputed questions of facts and defence of the accused cannot be taken into consideration at this pre-trial stage, which can be more appropriately gone into by the trial court at the appropriate stage.
7-At the stage of taking cognizance of the case and summoning the accused, the court below is not required to go into the merit and demerit of the case.
Genuineness or otherwise of the allegations cannot be even determined at the stage of summoning the accused.
8-This Court does not find that this case fall in a categories as recognized by the Apex Court for quashing the criminal proceeding of the trial Court at pre-trial stage.

Considering the facts,
circumstances and nature of allegations against the applicant in this case, the cognizable offence is made out.
At this stage it would not be appropriate to adjudge whether the case shall ultimately end in conviction or not.
Only prima facie satisfaction of the Court about the existence of sufficient ground to proceed in the matter is required.
The impugned criminal proceeding under the facts of this case cannot be said to be abuse of the process of the Court.
There is no good ground to invoke inherent power under Section 482 Cr.P.C. by this Court.
9-The relief as sought by the applicant through the instant application is hereby refused.
10-This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. lacks merit and is, accordingly, dismissed.
